notes:
Tables arrive on the dev channel, and syncing now updates the note you're actively editing — not just the ones in the background.

**New**

- **Tables (dev).** You can now build tables in your notes. Insert one with **/table** or from **Cmd+K → "Insert table"**, then edit cells, add or remove rows and columns, resize columns, set a header row, and align columns. Paste a table copied from a web page, a spreadsheet, or Markdown and it comes in as a real table; copy one out and it lands as clean Markdown **or** formatted HTML depending on where you paste it. Tables sync across your devices, and two devices editing **different cells** of the same table at the same time both keep their edits. (PRD Addendum 28 §Y — first-class table support across desktop and mobile.)

**Fixes & polish**

- **Live sync into the note you're editing.** When a sync pulls in changes, the note open on screen now updates in place — including the one your cursor is in — instead of only refreshing after a restart. Changes to the exact block you're typing in wait until you move your cursor away or pause, so nothing is yanked out from under you. (PRD Addendum 27 §X, Waves 2–3.)

**Under the hood**

- Remote sync changes are merged into the open editor with a **surgical block-diff transaction** (only changed blocks are patched, tagged so they don't echo back or pollute undo, and never applied mid-IME-composition) instead of a full note reload; the focused-note live-merge is behind the `live_sync_refresh` kill switch. (Addendum 27 §X; `blockDiffReconcile`.)
- Table edits converge across devices via a **position-keyed cell CRDT** — each cell is an independent last-writer-wins register carrying its own provenance — proven order-independent in the sync simulator; concurrent structural changes (row/column add-delete) fall back safely to whole-table last-writer-wins, and merged cells flatten to a plain grid for now. The Paper selection bar gained a table rule (§V3.6): a cell-rectangle selection paints per cell. (Addendum 28 §Y; ADR-0021.)
- Tables ride the `tables` gradual-rollout flag (on for dev) plus a kill switch; the table node is always registered so existing tables always render. A new DB migration (018) adds a side table for cell provenance.
